core_obligations: Reduce to the case where X is connected: the image of the component lies in a connected component X', and the component upstairs remains a connected component of the inverse image of X' (proof lines 1133-1135).
Establish the three topological properties of the projection when X is connected: it is open, closed and has finite fibres (proof lines 1136-1141).
Apply the topological lemma on open, closed maps with finite fibres to conclude that the image of the component is the whole of X, hence a connected component (proof lines 1142-1144).
difficulty_reason: For a finite extension of fields K/k and a scheme X over k, the lemma shows that the image of every connected component of the base change is a connected component of X (statement lines 1124-1130). The proof first traps the image inside a connected component X' of X, regards that component as a closed subscheme, and observes that the component upstairs is still a connected component of the inverse image of X', which reduces to the case where X is connected (proof lines 1133-1135). In that case the projection is open, closed and has finite fibres, since it is the base change of the universally open, universally closed and quasi-finite morphism from the spectrum of a field extension, and the topological lemma on finite-fibre maps then gives the conclusion (proof lines 1136-1144). The claim is H2: a reduction to the connected case plus the three structural properties of the projection, with the topological input doing the final step.
